atoms.b: The keyboard can be used to ((type)) words. There are different keys for letters, ((numbers)), punctuation marks and ((special)) characters.
Some ((keys)) can perform special functions. For example, the ((shift)) key allows us to type in ((capital)) letters.

atoms.text: Here are all the keys used to type letters. The keys aren’t arranged in alphabetical order. This means it can be difficult to find the letters quickly when you first start typing.
The number keys can be found in a row at the top of the keyboard. They all also have a punctuation mark or special character that can be typed by holding the shift key.

atoms.a: What do we use the shift key for?
b: ++to type some punctuation marks or special characters

instruction.text: When typing, three more special keys are particularly useful. Drag the correct names to each one.
Decide which key is needed for each task.

atoms.a: to put a space between two words
to start typing on a new line
to delete what has already been typed
